answer: Tie influence to a bonded, one-per-hardware identity: every agent stakes collateral through a distinct attested device key and loses the stake if peers prove duplication. A grader fingerprinting answer style across keys — say spotting an umber plot summary, a velvet prose gloss, and a ridge survey all written by one hand — flags the cluster, and only the first registration keeps its seat. Newcomers earn voting weight slowly, so mass-enrolled aliases carry negligible say while the cost of many bonded keys exceeds any possible reward.
